corrections.claim: KC_BUDGET bands (options 9-11; with DROP BUDGET 8 and SET slot 62 = 79): band 0 makes babies 'stop building traps' and 'stop cheese bites'; band 1 is 'traps on, cheese bites off'. Proposal (4) offers a 3-level head: 'no traps or bites / traps only / both'.
corrections.correction: Babies read BUDGET in exactly two places, and both are cat-only. tryBiteCat adds a 1-cheese boost to a cat bite when BUDGET*4 >= CHEESE_BITE_SURPLUS; the bite itself always happens. tryCatTrap skips a cat trap when BUDGET*4 < TRAP_SURPLUS, but only when the baby is not defending a king and not in coop. Rat traps and rat bites never read BUDGET (the rat-bite boost is finishCheese, which uses global cheese and FINISH_FLOOR). So no band can switch bites or rat traps off. Every band is a behavioural no-op when no cat is near, and for traps also during coop. BUDGET is also a raw net input, so a band edit mostly perturbs the inputs of the trainable nets.
corrections.evidence: Baby.java:802-803 (cat bite +1 cheese); Baby.java:846-850 (cat-trap gate, bypassed when defending or in coop); Baby.java:704-715 tryRatTrap (no BUDGET); Baby.java:764-765 and :786-790 (rat bite uses finishCheese). grep finds only these BUDGET reads: Baby.java:802, Baby.java:850, D.java:393, D.java:692, DK.java:796. King.java:83 rewrites BUDGET on every king turn.

corrections.claim: KC_DROP FORM (option 5) on a HOLD turn: 'babies see the formation as stale for that round (formSite needs FORM_T fresh 2)'.
corrections.correction: On a HOLD turn only FORM_T is pending, because F_HOLD writes FORM_T = stamp. DROP FORM reverts FORM_T to the turn-start snapshot, which is the king's previous HOLD stamp (age 1). fresh(t,2) accepts age <= 2, so babies acting after the king this round (age 1) and before the king next round (age 2) still see the formation. A single DROP FORM on a HOLD turn is therefore a behavioural no-op, an aliased option. Two consecutive drops hide the formation only from babies acting before the king in the following round; three hide it from everyone. The opening-turn desync claim is correct.
corrections.evidence: King.java:685-686 (F_HOLD writes only FORM_T); DK.java:696-699 (saPre snapshot, called at King.java:23); DK.java:815-817 (revert); Comms.java:46-50 (fresh is age <= maxAge); Baby.java:1528-1532 (formSite needs fresh(t,2)).

corrections.claim: KC_SET MINE slots (options 41-72) inside the list: 'Either way numMines changes for every reader and babies' mineTarget resets.'
corrections.correction: numMines changes only when a v=0 write to an x slot inside the list truncates the list. A nonzero x write, or any y write, inside the list turns a known mine into a phantom with numMines unchanged. refreshMine keys on the count, so it does not reset mineTarget, and babies already targeting that mine keep its old coordinates until they re-pick. The report also misses a case: a nonzero x written at index == numMines appends a phantom at once. Its y comes from whatever is in the paired slot (often 0, which gives y = -1), and numMines grows.
corrections.evidence: Comms.java:82-89 (readMines stops at the first x==0 and reads y from the paired slot); Comms.java:97-102 (addMine appends at numMines with no bounds check); Baby.java:1122-1125 (refreshMine keyed on the count).

corrections.claim: 'Exact replay: with floor 0 at 14 and 15 and KC_ZDB as the default, zdb replay is unchanged by construction', and floor 0 makes 'random comms corruption disappear'.
corrections.correction: Floor 0 does not make sampling deterministic. NET_T is a single global temperature of 1.0, and DNet.sample takes the argmax only when t <= 0 and floor <= 0; otherwise it samples from the softmax. With the calibrated init, where non-ZDB options sit at about -12, the softmax alone leaks about 4e-4 per KC record (measured p_top 0.9996; 72*e^-12 = 4.4e-4). At about 1,535 KC records per team-game, that is about 0.6-0.7 non-ZDB picks per team-game, roughly 8-9% of today's 7.8. Each SET or SQUEAK is then followed by uniform KING_VAL digits: point 15's logits are all zero, so its softmax is uniform whatever the floor. Exact replay needs the zdb-hard init (bias -30, the replay configuration in docs/decision-points.md:203, with --init-new zdb-hard and --floor-points 8:0,14:0,16:0) or a per-point argmax or scaled last layer. A global T=0 would change every other point too.
corrections.evidence: D.java:30 (NET_T = 1f, global); DNet.java:123 (argmax only if t<=0 && floor<=0); DNet.java:126-128 (softmax at t); dpnet_io.py:300-322 (calibrated delta ln(10*81/0.005) = 11.995); rl-m2 nets/0/net.json point-14 biases {0, -11.995}; devfb-cpi-x0.json point 14 p_top 0.9996.

corrections.claim: 'The per-point sensitivity build for 14 (sens14) was never run, so the cost of KING_COMMS deviations in games is not measured.' The same appears under 'cheap tests (b)'.
corrections.correction: zdph14 had been built and was running when the report was written: the plan listed KING_COMMS (14) as 'still running'. The run has since finished. At floor 0.2, KING_COMMS scored 19/64 = 0.297 against zdpg39 (t -3.74, 95% CI 0.199-0.418) and is classed sharp, alongside the baby tactics and KING_SPAWN. Random KC edits are therefore measured to be costly. That strengthens the case for protocol-safe KC exploration, and it undercuts the report's framing of KC as merely 'under-structured'.
corrections.evidence: docs/rl-es-plan.md:540 at ea0e56d ('MINE_PICK (7), BABY_FREE (8) and KING_COMMS (14) are still running'). Commit 33942ab: docs/rl-es-plan.md:540 'KING_COMMS (14) | 19/64 = 0.30 | -3.7 | sharp'; diagnostics/zdp-action-space/sensitivity.json:153 (package zdph14, score 0.2969, lo 0.199, hi 0.4177).

corrections.claim: KING_COMMS missing information: 'the exact round (round/10 only, so stamp freshness cannot be computed)', 'the king's local state (Sym.mask ... whether a formation is open)'.
corrections.correction: KC opens right after King.publish has written the king's heartbeat stamp and the merged Sym.mask. So the 64 raw-slot features hold Sym.mask exactly (raw slot 1). They hold round&1023 exactly in the king's own heartbeat slot KING0+3*slot+2, indexed by the slot feature, which is the same route the report accepts for y. For the formation king, a formation held this turn shows as FORM_T equal to its own stamp. The information is present but needs an indexing or equality decode that an MLP will find hard; it is not absent. KC has neither me.x nor me.y as direct features, while KV has me.x but not me.y. For KING_VAL, the round&1023 and me.y gaps are real.
corrections.evidence: King.java:168-175 (publish writes x+1, y+1, stamp, then SYM = merged mask); King.java:82-85 (publish happens before the KC opens); DK.java:743 (raw slots); DK.java:755 (slot feature); DK.java:762-786 (KV features).

corrections.claim: KC_ALERT_CALL (12) and SET ALERT (34, 35): 'For 3 rounds, babies within ALERT_DIST2 225 and beyond d2 8 walk to the king (Baby.java:1283-1288), babies within DEFEND_D2 defend it'.
corrections.correction: The rally is the last branch of war(). zdb's cascade calls war() only when !G.coop, and only after role ATTACK. Inside war(), a GATHER baby that is not hunting and has no threatened king returns at once; only an adjacent enemy stops it. The eKing and nearest-enemy branches also take precedence over the rally. So under zdb's cascade the rally moves only non-gatherers or hunting gatherers, and only outside coop. Calls and clears made during coop change nothing in zdb's cascade. In net mode the M_WAR executor calls war() with no coop check, so the net can trigger the rally during coop through BABY_MOVE. Defense needs !coop, a fresh-2 alert and threat >= 1, and ALERT_CALL always forces threat >= 1.
corrections.evidence: Baby.java:1037 (!G.coop && war()); Baby.java:1249-1255 (gatherer early return); Baby.java:1256-1282 (earlier branches); Baby.java:1283-1288 (rally); Baby.java:1297-1301 (threatenedKing); Baby.java:2371-2373 (net M_WAR calls war() unconditionally); DK.java:851 (max(1,t)).

corrections.claim: KING_VAL: 'About 360 of the 425 sampled KING_VAL rows are SET digits (2 per sampled SET)'.
corrections.correction: Frozen-point rows are sampled at 5% per record, independently of their parent KC record, so KV rows are not 2 per sampled KC SET. From the KC totals, about 3,600 SETs give 7,200 digits, about 20 SQUEAKs give 140 and about 20 RMs give 20. About 98% of KV rows are therefore SET digits, roughly 415 of 425. In other words, KING_VAL data is almost entirely raw slot values.
corrections.evidence: rl_data.py:211-216 (per-record frozen sample); cpi-x0-summary.json point 14 option_hist (SET 180 of 199 sampled non-ZDB picks); DK.java:859 (squeak: D.digits(32,1,...), 7 digits); DK.java:868 (RM: 1 digit); DK.java:876 (SET: 2 digits).

corrections.claim: DROP_ALL and DROP SLOT: '3 consecutive silent turns remove the king from numKings for every reader'; 'One use is a one-round delay'. Proposal (2) uses 'hide' for 3 or more uses.
corrections.correction: readKings needs a heartbeat age <= 2. After drops in rounds r and r+1, the slot keeps stamp r-1, so robots acting before the king in round r+2 already see age 3 and lose the king (for example from nearestKing for cheese delivery). Two consecutive drops are enough for that, and three hide the king from everyone. A single drop leaves the heartbeat fresh (age 1). It does republish last round's x/y if the king moved, and it skips the SYM publish. So the effect depends on turn order, and the 'hide' threshold is 2 turns, not 3.
corrections.evidence: Comms.java:46-50; Comms.java:58-66 (readKings fresh 2); King.java:168-170 (heartbeat written every turn); DK.java:815-817 (revert to the snapshot).

corrections.claim: 'No learned weights are lost, because 14 and 15 have never been trained.' 'Training 14 failed at rl-m2 iteration 0 (KL 6 after one step) ... the cause was raw-scale hidden activations, which reinit_new_points.py fixes, but 14 and 15 have stayed frozen ever since.' Also: 'the net is a constant function ... zero last layer'.
corrections.correction: After the reinit fix (commit 7b7b2fb, '14,16 trainable again'), point 14 was trained in rl-m2 iteration 1: v1 to v2, 172 PPO steps on 348,770 rows, KL to the anchor 0.055, no alarms. v2's point-14 net is not constant: last-layer |w| goes up to 0.26, the option-0 bias is -0.0195, and the other biases range from -12.03 to -11.86. Point 14 was frozen at iteration 2 for a different reason: its KL to the anchor jumped from 0.055 to 0.59 between iterations (commit be65c46). rl_train copies frozen points value-for-value from the learner net, and no later rollback is recorded. So v39's KC net is this once-trained, state-dependent net, not the calibrated constant. The configs/rl-m2.json purpose text and docs/rl-es-plan.md:545 ('never trained') are stale. Point 15 was never in rl-m2's trainable list, so the claim is correct for 15. In practice little is lost (KL 0.055). But making 14 trainable means handling this instability, not only the init scale.
corrections.evidence: git log -- configs/rl-m2.json: c528e89, then 7b7b2fb, then be65c46. The rl-m2 nets are in the scratchpad at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-terryvanbelle-projects-vibe-bc26a0/31310128-fb77-4058-8e53-1da41e55d47b/scratchpad/critic_dl/runs/rl/rl-m2/nets/. nets/2/metrics.json, point 14: steps 172, used 348770, kl_anchor_end 0.055, changed true. nets/2/net.json against nets/0, nets/1 and dbg1416/m2/anchor, which all have a zero last layer and biases {0, -11.995}. nets/1/ROLLBACK.json says 'KL collapse refusal at iter 0'. rl_train.py:42 and :443 copy frozen points unchanged.

missed: KC edits are input noise for the trainable nets, not only protocol corruption. The baby comms block cb (R0-R2, raw BUDGET, ALERT age/threat/distance, FORM age; D.java:686-702) is appended at BABY_MOVE (D.java:324), BABY_ACT_PRE/POST (D.java:446, plus raw BUDGET at D.java:393), BABY_ROLE (D.java:549), BABY_COMMS (D.java:634), BABY_FREE (D.java:767) and BABY_VAL (D.java:794). BABY_ROLE, which is trainable, also reads all 64 raw slots (D.java:550), plus numKings, numMines and the Sym counts (D.java:523-540). Kings read kmini at points 10-13 (DK.java:156, 214, 287, 340; D.java:705-709). Uniform 0..1023 SET values push these inputs outside the imitation distribution. This is the same mechanism as the BABY_ROLE input-27 poisoning already documented in docs/rl-es-plan.md:579-585.

Several KC options are aliased no-ops in common states, yet entropy and the KL leash count them as distinct actions (rl_train.py:286-294). Examples: a single DROP FORM on a HOLD turn; a single DROP SLOT or DROP_ALL (the heartbeat stays fresh); ALERT_CALL, ALERT_CLEAR and SET ALERT during coop (zdb skips war(), Baby.java:1037); BUDGET bands with no cat nearby, and for traps also during coop (Baby.java:802, 850).

When a KC executor fails or a digit raises dfail mid-chain, the parent KC record is dropped (DK.java:832, D.point=0). The KING_VAL digit records already emitted through D.digits (D.java:803-820) stay in the data as orphans: their own logq is trained, while the choice that caused them is lost.

D.fallback flags a fallback only when zdb's label differs from k (D.java:159-162, l != k). If k cannot act but zdb's cascade happens to choose the same label, the flag is 0. The fallback rates in devfb and the summary are therefore lower bounds.

R0-R2 (the REG group, slots 20-22) are not free. King.java:143-146 overwrites them as EKING whenever a king hears any type-3 squeak, and baby C_RAW raw squeaks (Baby.java:2167-2172) can send type 3 as well as KC_SQUEAK. So DROP REG is reachable, and the free registers in proposal (8) would be overwritten by baby noise unless the type nibble is masked for every raw squeak.

claimSlot falls back to slot 0 when no slot is stale (King.java:16), so two kings can share slot 0. They then share the heartbeat and the formation writes gated on slot 0 (King.java:670), which breaks the 'own heartbeat' decode and makes FORM pending ambiguous.

KC runs after the king's own actions and after zdb's writes for the turn (King.java:82-87). zdb rewrites the heartbeat, SYM, BUDGET (King.java:83) and FORM_T (King.java:686) on every turn. Any value the net writes into a zdb-maintained field therefore lasts only until the next king turn. The net cannot own such a field persistently, so a policy channel must live in slots zdb never writes.
overall_reliability: Reliable on code mechanics and on the measurements. About 55 of the 65 claims I checked hold, including every count taken from devfb-cpi-x0.json and cpi-x0-summary.json, and most file:line citations; a few are off by 1-4 lines, e.g. rl_data.py:250 should be :254 and dpnet_io.py:296-304 should be :300-322. Several substantive errors would mislead a redesign. First, BUDGET gates only non-defensive, non-coop cat traps and the +1 cheese on cat bites, not 'traps and bites'. Second, a DROP FORM on a HOLD turn is a no-op, not a stale formation. Third, 'floor 0 gives exact replay by construction' is false: the global T=1 softmax still leaks about 0.6 KC picks per team-game. Fourth, writes into the MINE list do not always change numMines. Fifth, sens14 did run: it scored 0.30 and is classed sharp, while the report says it was never measured. Sixth, point 14 was trained once and is not a constant function. Seventh, some 'missing information' (Sym.mask, the exact stamp, formation-open) is present in KC's raw-slot features, though hard to decode. The largest omission is that KC's random edits also perturb the inputs of the trainable nets: BABY_ROLE reads all 64 raw slots, and the cb block and the BUDGET feature feed points 1-3, 5, 6, 8 and 9. KC noise is therefore input noise for RL as well as corruption of zdb's protocol. Line numbers were checked against HEAD (ea0e56d/33942ab; the zdp sources are unchanged since f6e4dd7). The working tree now has uncommitted floorWeights edits by another agent in D.java, DK.java, DNet.java and W.java, which shift DK.java lines after 359 by +1.
proposal_concerns: The alternative fix, 'record the executed option and train on the aliased action', needs that action's behaviour probability: the sum of p over every option that would have produced the same behaviour in that state. Computing it needs the same can-act predicates for every option as masking before sampling, so it reduces to the first fix. rl_data also keeps only k and logq(k), never the label (rl_data.py:218-222).

Floor 0 at 14 and 15 alone gives neither exact replay nor a KC free of noise. T=1 is global (D.java:30, DNet.java:123), and the calibrated biases near -12 still leak about 0.6 KC picks per team-game, each followed by uniform KV digits. Use the zdb-hard init (-30) or a per-point argmax. Read zfree (zdpz) with this in mind: its KC is quieter but not silent.

The BUDGET policy register in proposal (4) must be built around what BUDGET actually gates: non-defensive, non-coop cat traps and the +1 cheese on cat bites (Baby.java:802, 850). Alternatively, new baby gates could deliberately extend it to rat traps and bites. The 'no traps or bites' level does not exist today.

The DROP FORM / 'defer' redesign in proposal (2) must cover the HOLD phase. There one drop is a no-op, two drops hide the formation from babies acting before the king, and three hide it from all. The meaning of 'defer' differs between open, hold and close, and the heartbeat 'hide' takes 2 turns, not 3.

The free registers R0-R2 in proposal (8) are overwritten on any heard type-3 squeak (King.java:143-146), including the babies' C_RAW squeaks. Either remove the SQ_EKING handling or mask zdb types for every raw squeak, baby squeaks included and not only KC_SQUEAK.

Repacking zdb's schema to free slots changes the meaning of BABY_ROLE's 64 raw-slot inputs (D.java:550) and of the cb and kmini blocks. Point 5 is trainable and RL-trained, so 'no learned weights are lost' holds only if the slot layout stays fixed. Any change to KC features or options also needs dimension changes in widen and build_dpnet.
Typed heads with floor 0 and very negative logits hit the QMAX cap on logq (D.java:144-145, q capped at 65535), as the report itself notes. Keep a small per-group floor or widen q.

Making KC trainable again must handle its observed instability. After the init fix, one iteration reached KL 0.055 to the anchor, and the next jumped to 0.59 and was refused (be65c46). With 81 options and a KL leash to a near-constant anchor, rare options produce large ratio swings. Typed heads with few options per group would help here.

The typed ALERT rally head in proposal (5) only moves babies that zdb routes through war(): outside coop, and non-gatherers or hunting gatherers, after war()'s higher-priority branches (Baby.java:1037, 1249-1288). Only BABY_MOVE's net M_WAR bypasses the coop check. Rally behaviour needs a matching baby-side decision, or the king-side head will mostly be a no-op.
